## core-dump: end-of-week halt after gcc-map v4 follow-through (gcc-map-7e, 2026-09-05 17:35)

**Purpose:** full checkpoint for a session that finished one stream (gcc-map v4 batch, uncommitted) and planned a second (pivotal docs review) whose adversarial review died with a process restart.

**Insights:**

1. A process restart kills in-process seats and wipes the session scratchpad, but subagent transcripts under `projects/<slug>/<sid>/subagents/` survive. Check the transcript's longest assistant text block before declaring a seat's work lost; here it showed the seat had died on its first line, so the task went back to pending honestly.
2. The template literal `AGENT: none — go` trips the prose gate on Write. Use `AGENT: none, go`.
3. `ls` of the atone verdicts directory with options after the path fails under zsh; put options first or use `rg` on the directory listing.
4. When the owner asks for the task table at halt time, render it from `task-table.sh` first and reset any row whose seat died before believing the store's "running".

## validate: second seat on task #59 refuted a class claim the ledger could not see · 2026-09-05 16:15
**Purpose:** Route the validation of #59 (renderer clips, empty meter, wrapped title) and record what the second seat found.

**Insights:**
1. A parity ledger built from the call sites the change touched cannot fail on a call site it never listed. The seat found a fourth hard slice on the --refs path by grepping the whole file for the pattern class; the author's ledger had ten rows and none covered --refs. Grep the file for the class before claiming the class closed.
2. "Proven by mutation" must say where the mutant lives. Mutants run from a scratch script are real proof of the moment, not a guard the suite carries; the row's note conflated the two and the seat read it as false. Name the mechanism in the claim.
3. The seat's Vg answer was worth the dispatch on its own: it named that this row makes the page tell fewer lies while the owner's complaint is about looks, which is the colour call the owner has not yet ruled. A validator that only checks the rows never says that.

## catchup: resumed the /tasks re-eval, landed #54 #55 #56 and the audit's V1/V2 · 2026-09-05 13:40
**Purpose:** Resume from the full dump, build the three prepared rows, and run the owner's mid-turn ask for a cold visual audit of /tasks, re-lensed for a person with six tabs.

**Insights:**
1. The "resolved by content-match" mislabel had a mechanism, not a wording problem: resolve-store.sh rung 1 returned any store NAMED for the live session, empty included, and the ladder called every resolver answer a content match. Fix the rung and the label together or the wording fix lies again next resume.
2. A visual audit seat needs a frozen copy of the renderer, because the parent edits the live file while the seat renders; the frozen copy also made the seat's captures reproducible after the fix landed.
3. An audit by one careful cold reader ranks empty chrome first; the same audit re-lensed for a tab-flipping owner drops it to third and puts tab identity and the owed surface first. Ask for the reader's situation in the brief, not after.
4. A line claimed inside the body after the last box is gone half the time, because the row loop fills to the cap; anything that must appear when the screen is full belongs in the footer on a line the fixed point reserved.
5. Case 9's corner mutation is sensitive to band order: re-measure the deciding fixture size after any change to what leads a box (the table is in its comment).
6. The band-order mutation in a suite must target the expensive band SECOND; the box prices its first band atomically, so a mutant on the band check has nothing to bite if the costly band leads.

## gcc-map: deep v4 structure map with visual sheets [gcc-map-3e], 2026-09-05 12:20

**Purpose:** Second `--deep` map of `~/.claude`: measure load channels and the doc graph before reading the indices, diff, run the battery plus the four checks v3 proposed, fan out five lens seats and a critic, write MAP.md and a d3 companion page.

**Insights:**

1. Read the session's own injected UserPromptSubmit context as evidence first. The top finding (four `hinters/*.test.sh` files executing on every prompt) was visible in the first prompt's hint block as `pass=8 fail=0` lines; measuring it later cost one `ls -l`.
2. Verify lens headline claims against the file before folding them in. One lens claim (the fable sentinel lifting a second check) died on a single `rg -B3 -A3`; another (per-skill runtime-notes references broken) was reversed by a sibling lens reading the guard clause. Both would have shipped as findings.
3. The regenerated indices were exactly right and every hand-maintained one had drifted, same as v3. Skip re-verifying `rules/00-index.md` and `skills/00-index.md` row by row next time; spend the calls on FOLDERS, NAMESPACE, LOOKUP, MIGRATIONS.
4. The chrome-devtools MCP profile was held by another session; Playwright worked but blocks `file://`, needs an `http://` origin (claim a 62xx port with `ports.sh claim <name> --tier 3`, `free` it after) and only writes screenshots under `~/.claude/.playwright-mcp/`.
5. The artifact gate blocks publishing when the owner asked for visuals but not a hosted page. Write the HTML into the report dir and offer publishing in one line; do not retry the publish.
6. Run `validate_palette.js` before drawing: the first hand-picked palette failed three checks in both themes; the reference palette's first four slots passed on the page's own surfaces in one run each.
7. The `git ls-tree` series the churn lens produced (always-on bytes at five revisions) is the right growth instrument; the parent's two-point v3-vs-now comparison hid that the 09-01 diet never brought the total below its pre-diet mark.

## core-dump: full dump at 96% context after the /tasks and /goal re-eval · 2026-09-05 10:40
**Purpose:** Hand a fresh window the exact remainder (#54 #55 #56) with the parity ledger and the six owner calls, after a night of landing defaults across wakes.

1. Three mini dumps with addenda carried the session through 82% to 96% context; the full dump at the end consolidated their caveats by hand because the stem-based caveat diff cannot match a mini to a full.
2. The wake loop kept working at 85-95% context by landing one contained, suite-guarded piece per fire and refusing multi-file changes; the one crash came from a heredoc edit launched into suites without a smoke render, now a standing constraint.

**Purpose:** Checkpoint the /tasks and /goal re-eval at the boundary where two adversarial seats were the only work in flight.

**Insights:**

Second live instance in one night (first: the fabad34c checkpoint). **Purpose:** Build /deploy-parity-testing from a notes file the dispatcher wrote first (walmart-on-foundry phases 2 to 4), spec-first, one review seat.

**Insights:**

1. Writing the planning and execution notes as their own file BEFORE invoking create-skill made the skill a compression pass instead of a recall pass; the seat found zero pasted input from the owner because the owner's words never entered the draft.
2. The seat's real catch was a worked example frozen as a requirement: four off-box rows from one project written as THE table. Fix was to name the class each row belongs to and label the four as one derivation. Same shape as examples-as-quotas, one level up.

## session: catchup forge-console walmart kickoff [catch-forge-9a / forge-console] — 2026-09-03

Purpose: resume forge-console off the 13:30 dump for the walmart buildout, flaw-pass first.

Insights:
- The cron ledger keys liveness on the harness pid, and /clear keeps the pid. A cron cancelled before the /clear therefore still reads LIVE in the ledger; CronList is the instrument for "armed in this process", the ledger only says "the process that armed it is alive". Check both before re-arming.
- The compound collector command (cron-duty + pm2 + curl + kanban + goal in one line) was denied by the permission layer; the same five as separate calls all ran. Split collectors from the start.
- The local runner pm2 name is foundry-runner after the rename; it was stopped and came up on `pm2 start foundry-runner` with /health 200 in four seconds.

## session: repo audit across six axes, nothing changed [audit-pick-7a] · 2026-09-03

**Purpose:** owner asked for a self-written audit brief (usability, completeness, consistency, waste, discoverability, agent self-serve) over every category in the repo, run inline. Brief and report under `.claude/output/20260903-repo-audit/`, decision page `vb-repo-audit-0903` for the eight owner calls.

**Insights:**
1. zsh does not word-split an unquoted variable: `n scripts/$s` with `s="check-citations.mjs docs"` hands node ONE argument and reads as `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Three scripts looked broken for a turn; none were. Split the loop variable or use an array.
2. The showcase registry keys on `href`, not `slug`; a sweep on `slug:` returns zero and every dependent check goes silently wrong. Read the entry shape (lines 41 to 62) before writing a sweep against it.
3. `pm2 restart playground-dev` said the process did not exist, though CONTRIBUTING and AGENTS both say it runs there. `pm2 start "fnm exec --using 24 -- pnpm dev -p 5104" --name playground-dev` from `apps/playground` brought it up; it is not `pm2 save`d.
4. The agent-facing measures that mattered: props declared vs named in the contract doc (376 of 380), snippets with an import line (3 of 33), the awareness prompt's hard-coded "both apps" claim. Heading presence alone would have passed the docs.
5. The owner's mid-turn steer: the showcase UI is the check, not the subject; components, patterns and docs an agent uses are the subject. Weight the next audit that way from the brief.

## core-dump: aep-flat-49 — 2026-09-03 02:35

**Purpose:** Checkpointed the AEP Catalog V9 flattening session (transform, review, cleanup, push).

**Insights:**

1. The parse-contract validator passed first try because the template headings were copied verbatim rather than paraphrased. Copying beats remembering here.
2. The caveat-diff step correctly no-op'd: stem `aep-flat-49` had no prior dump. Matching by name stem rather than session uuid is what made the skip silent-and-correct instead of falsely comparing against another session's file.
3. `goal.sh show` reported `harness /goal: not armed (last /goal was clear)`, which is the auto-clear on a MET goal, not an unset one. Recording it as MET rather than `none` preserves the distinction a resume needs.
4. Two hooks shaped the write: the prose gate rejected a single em-dash that lived inside a quoted DATA value, fixed by backticking the quote; and the commit-trailer gate blocked the harness-requested Co-Authored-By lines, where the gcc ruling wins.
5. A style-watch fire against PLAN.md was real (16 decorative bold spans on numbers) and was acted on before the dump, then logged with `--heeded yes`.

## session: gcc-audit resume, halt-imbalance fix [0fb48af0] — 2026-09-01
Purpose: resume from _20260901-gcc-audit.claude.md and deliver the checkpoint's top pending item.
- Owner armed the checkpoint's proposed goal mid-catchup; treat that as the pick, no hand-off question needed.
- The checkpoint's "measurement in <path>" citation pointed at a report that never carried the 14-vs-2 number. A checkpoint citation needs the same grep-before-believing as any other; re-derived (15-vs-2) with a persisted artifact + scan.sh before fixing.
- Fix followed the survival finding (decidable lands, judgment doesn't): one uniform greppable clause at each halt site + a validator gate, not more judgment prose. Guard mutation-tested red/green.
- task.sh add rejects --tags; use --domain/--class. task-table --pin prints no table by design.

**Purpose:** Spacing/margin/link round after the owner opened the doc in Google Docs, plus first confirmed Drive delivery.

**Insights:**
1. Google Docs ignores paragraph-border `w:space` padding more than Word: a rail TOC needs real `w:ind` distance from the bar, not border spacing, and hyperlink underline+bright-secondary reads terrible on a linked TOC. Links are now accent, no underline, by ruling.
2. Margins ruled to half inch; footer/header margins must shrink with them (360 twips) or the footer collides with the body.
3. Drive delivery confirmed working via rclone `--drive-import-formats docx`; remote auto-detected (owner's is `versable`), default folder `Docs` ruled correct, never ask for a path first.

---

**Purpose:** Owner-ruled theme promoted to spec: theme.json beside render.py, auto-loaded; ruled over decision pages doc-style/-2/-3.

**Insights:**
1. Pandoc's docx writer reorders XML attributes in styles.xml, so test assertions on style XML must be attribute-order-agnostic (`<w:insideH[^/]*w:val="dashed"`), never adjacent-pair literals.
2. The ruled callout layout is two paragraphs (Head style + body style) sharing identical pBdr+shd so Word merges them into one visual block; Head keeps-next, after=0, body before=0.
3. LibreOffice's preview renders a dashed frame but underdraws the solid left accent bar on the same paragraph; trust Word for mixed border styles, note it in the delivery.
4. Google Doc delivery: rclone remote + `--drive-import-formats docx` converts on upload; auth is a one-time human `rclone config`, refresh token durable. Helper: scripts/word-doc/gdrive-upload.sh

---

**Purpose:** Convert a repo doc (docs/what-is-where.md, estate overview) to docx preserving links, tables, tree diagram.

**Insights:**
1. A source doc whose H1 moved to frontmatter needs all headings promoted one level, or preflight warns "first heading is not level 1"; promote H3 before H2 to avoid double-promotion.
2. A hyphenated compound broken across source lines ("committed-and-\nfenced") renders as a broken hyphen in the docx; the page check catches it, grep for "-\n" beforehand next time.
3. A 12-heading doc with 6 sibling tables takes the static TOC well; 6 pages, no layout defects on first real-content render.

---

**Purpose:** Build /recommend, the four-block answer to "what now": the call, gates clearable today with drafted answers, defaults applied, path to the next checkpoint.

**Insights:**

1. The intent seat earned its keep for the third recorded run. Its best catch was not style: Validation check 1 (gate precision) could never execute, because the ledger call fires in the same turn that raises the gates, before the owner has answered them. No allowed-tools change fixes that; it is a timing defect, not a capability one. Resolved by having the skill grade its PREDECESSOR at the start of each run, which suits a skill that is invoked repeatedly.
2. Second catch worth carrying: `skill-log.sh --corrections` already exists for "user corrections that followed" and the draft hardcoded it to 0 while burying the real count in free-text `--note`, which `list` cannot aggregate. Check for an existing structured field before inventing a `--metrics` shape.
3. I independently found defect 1 one turn before the seat reported, and still got the weaker fix (a new two-record metrics protocol) where the seat found the stronger one (the field already there). Self-review found the problem; the fresh seat found the cheaper answer.
4. A skill about restraint is the easiest place to over-write. Three sentences in the draft editorialised about the skill's own importance ("This phase is the skill", "the sharpest test in the list") and gated nothing. The Brief sat at exactly 8 content lines against an under-eight bar, and cutting the rhetoric fixed both at once.

## session: kanban UI sweep, ideation cut, usage trial, prosecution [gcc-kanban 4bbe4cbd] — 2026-08-26

**Purpose:** resume after /clear, finish the queue, then three sub-agent rounds (fable ideation, sonnet usage trial, opus adversarial prosecution).

- The PreCompact hook clobbered a fresh /core-dump by symlinking over `_checkpoint.claude.md`. Filed prop-20260825-094950-28. The dump's index summary line survived and was the only thing that made the resume possible.
- Four instrument-lies in one session, all reading as passes: a regex matching `>` after `esc()` had already made it `&gt;`; `ls` on a permission-denied dir printing "total 0"; a keyboard test whose expected value was already set; a grep matching my own prose inside the rendered document.
- `KANBAN_ROOT` is honoured by the server, which let the adversarial prosecutor drive a real instance on :6222 against copied data rather than the live board. That resolves the standing conflict between "execute to test drag" and "never mutate live state".
- Writing the check before the thing it checks caught real bugs both times: the board auditor had the exact counting bug it exists to catch, and the claims ledger forced admitting zero drags were performed all session.
- zsh does not word-split unquoted variables. `$K tag ...` where `K="bash kanban.sh"` failed silently for a whole batch that reported success.

## Skill: skills batches 1-3 (gcc-night-7a) · 2026-08-27 00:40
**Purpose:** Owner rulings skills-0826 D1a-D6a: parked band, subagent-prompt mode, persona dispatch primitive, routers as hand-offs.
**Insights:**
- zsh does not word-split an unquoted `$LIST` in `for s in $LIST`; a safety check and a move both ran once over the whole string and reported "parked 0" while looking successful. Loops over word lists go in a `bash` heredoc.
- `skills-parked/` with `parked.sh` already existed (2026-08-20); the roster only lacked a Parked heading in `skills/00-index.md` and a pick-skill that searches both files. 21 more parked (32 total), 69 live.
- 151 sub-agent briefs in 7 days; the ones that worked share a hand-grown vocabulary (Read first, Input, Scope, Hard rules, Do not touch, Output, Return only, Write before returning, Scope close). The subagent-prompt mode keeps those names and seeds structure by goal shape (build, review, judge, plan, research, digest).
- Five personas mined from the real role openers of the week (hands-lane, ui-reviewer, planning-seat, fresh-context-judge, digest-seat); `persona.sh seat` composes and logs a dispatch, which is the only persona path telemetry shows converting.

## Skill: ipc wake rung built and drilled (gcc-night-7a) · 2026-08-26 18:50
**Purpose:** Owner ruling 1a: a reply-by request to an idle session creates a headless turn. Built `warden/ipc-wake.sh`, pm2 `ipc-wake`, armed.
**Insights:**
- `claude-ipc digest` is scoped to the invoking cwd's project; a machine-wide reader must walk every peer cwd and merge. Discovered when the drill session was invisible from ~/.claude.
- The broker marks a session idle only after 300s without heartbeat (`CLAUDE_IPC_IDLE_S`); a wake rung cannot fire faster than that, and a just-registered session reads live. Drill waits must account for it.
- `jq fromdate` rejects `+00:00`; use `fromdateiso8601` on the raw `Z` timestamp. The hourly-cap guard passed green while broken until the test forced it red.
- A `-p` session does not register an alias by itself; `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=<sid> claude-ipc register <alias>` from its cwd puts it on the roster with the right cwd.
---

---

## Skill: ward-revive built and drilled (gcc-night-7a) · 2026-08-26 16:25
**Purpose:** Implement REMEDY-PLAN P1+P2+P3 (session-state.sh, ward-revive.sh behind `.revive-armed`, wake/goal payload contract) after a structural recon of the checkpoint.
**Insights:**
- `claude -p --resume` runs in the INVOKER's cwd. Any supervisor resuming another session must `cd` into that session's cwd first (goal `.cwd`, else the transcript's).
- A resumed ward obeys a standing "do not use tools" line in its own context over a new payload. Seed drills neutrally; expect real wards carrying stand-down text to ignore revives.
- Alive must mean a tool call inside the window, never transcript mtime: an ALIVE-only turn is the disease and would otherwise reset the clock.
- Two instruments the prior session's ledger marked validated (`skill-census3.py`, `probe-turnsource.py`) were never on disk. The ledger recorded intent, not files.
- `warden/warden-beat.test.sh` fails 8/11 on its own: its fixture sessions are past the 24h liveness cut.

## session: portal UI batch + passport SSO cutover + plan batch E/B/D/A [catch-port-b2] — 2026-08-25

Purpose: ship the owner's nexus feedback, cut tech.versable.ai over to passport SSO, write the planning lane for the next opus session.

Insights:
- wrangler-action@v3 runs wrangler 3.90 unless `wranglerVersion` is set; unknown wrangler.toml keys are dropped with a warning, `run_worker_first` among them. Read the deploy log before trusting a gate.
- The owner's push sentinel has to be touched in a real terminal; a `! touch` in the prompt arrives as chat text.
- Two listeners on one port (a stale http.server from a prior session on 127.0.0.1, mine on ::) made `curl localhost` and the browser disagree; `lsof -iTCP:<port>` before trusting a preview.
- Versable Internal has no passport sign-out and its /logout is POST-only, so app sign-out must land on an ungated page or it re-enters silently.
- When the owner assigns a fable planning seat, do the planning in it; three opus seats were dispatched and stopped.
- file-tools http_request is the sanctioned path when the classifier denies shell curl on an auth flow.

- Two measurement bugs the same day had one shape: the suite tested the path
  that does not run in production. The carry-over suite and the telemetry suite
  both covered the fallback branch while production takes the summary branch.
  A fixture chosen by whoever wrote the check exercises the branch they had in
  mind.
- Recognise a thing by what it declares, never by the shape it happens to have.
  A shape test for "is this a real review" threw away the findings of every
  comment predating a title rename. Two markers cost one line and cannot be
  wrong.
- A silent review and a dead pipeline looked identical for a day. Any surface
  that can legitimately say nothing needs to say something instead, or its
  silence is unreadable.
- A finding and its remedy are separate claims. Across five bot findings, all
  five diagnoses were right and two remedies were wrong, and every weak remedy
  concerned code the model had to imagine rather than read.
- Confirm a mutation actually applied. Two of mine were no-ops from bad shell
  escaping and stayed green, which reads exactly like a passing guard.
- `--effort` was set on no seat in any workflow. The knob nobody had touched
  was the one worth turning.

## session: tech nexus build + public-Pages closure nexus-b4d4 — 2026-08-13

Purpose: get three private repos publishing docs to one gated hostname, then fix
everything the owner found wrong with it.

Insights:
- A private repo's GitHub Pages site is public unless the plan carries Pages
  access control, and Team does not. walmart-mvp served its docs to anyone for
  months after the workflow that built them was retired. Retiring a publisher
  stops the refresh, not the serving.
- GitHub Pages has three settings that must agree: `build_type` (`workflow`
  ignores `source.branch` entirely), the source branch, and whether a build was
  ever requested. Changing the source alone succeeds and does nothing.
- Cloudflare Access answers before the asset layer, so no HTTP status from a
  gated host distinguishes a real page from a missing one, signed in or out.
- A local `python3 -m http.server` returns 200 with a directory listing exactly
  where Cloudflare returns 404. Status checks against a local rebuild prove
  nothing; content checks do.
- `head -N file > new && cat block >> new` looks like an edit and behaves like a
  truncation. It silently dropped a deploy safety guard and the syntax check
  still passed.
- Order destructive sequences so the guard runs before the exposure. A mid-script
  422 aborted before a CNAME removal that was the only thing keeping a private
  repo's tree off the public internet.

## session: pr-board build (automation-85ae630d, 2026-08-11)

Purpose: stand up the GitHub-to-Slack PR board (first automation in this repo).

Key locations:

  https://github.com/organizations/versable-git/settings/apps/pr-review-automation
- Private key: `pr-board/pr-review-automation.private-key.pem` (gitignored; the
  `~/Documents` original was verified identical and trashed 2026-08-12; if ever
  lost, generate a fresh key on the App settings page)
- Slack list: F0BP8DHA0S0 in #pr-review (C0BLN0QQGJW); bot user `pr_automation`
- Local secrets: `pr-board/.env` (gitignored)

Insights:

- Architecture (owner decision 2026-08-11): idempotent upsert receiver on Render
  free tier, plus an external /healthz pinger, plus a daily Actions sweep that
  redelivers failed webhook deliveries, prunes rows, and keeps itself enabled.
  No reconcile cron. GitHub's 3-day delivery ledger is the self-heal state.
- Slack Lists API: writes reject `value` and `text`; each column type has a
  typed carrier (rich_text blocks, link:[{original_url}], number:[int], select
  by option id). Reads spell link keys camelCase (`originalUrl`). On writes,
  `list_not_found` means the share is read-only, not that the id is wrong.
- Schema validation runs before permission checks, so payload shapes can be
  probed without write access: `invalid_arguments` means bad shape,
  `list_not_found` means the shape is fine and only permission is missing.
- Owner ruled against hosting the pinger in enhancement-product's notify cron
  (PR #189): keep this product's uptime independent of another product's
  pipeline. Finish PR #189 separately.

**Purpose:** Fix the decision-page wake for real (owner correction x2), build the ruled residue-review/speculative-atone system, and close its first live loop on this very session.

**Insights:**

1. The wake was never broken; it was never armed. The chip said "arm in THIS turn" twice and was read as decoration. Juror: very-wrong, aggravated by the repeat. The mechanical fix is the chip now printing the paste-ready watcher command, and the server pushing ipc as a --service identity.
2. claude-ipc identity is contextual: registering a name from the agent's shell binds it to the agent's session (making the server's push a self-send); daemons need `register <name> --service`. The broker's own refusals name the fix at each step; read them before patching.
3. The residue auditor's first real run nominated its own author 10 times; 4 survived confirm (incl. the wake S3), 6 died to cited refutations. The confirm/refute asymmetry (real mist id required; 40+ char evidence required) made both paths honest.
4. Never retry an append-only write on the evidence of your own parser: three duplicate dense-briefing events came from a regex that ate successful ids ([0-9-] misses hex). Check the ledger before retrying (mist-20260819-233248-d6).
5. ledger_id collides in bursts (2-hex tail, 1s resolution) — both new CLIs now loop until unique; any future ledger writer should.

## session: coverage build (callouts, parking, prototypes, seat) [valid-docx-7a] — 2026-08-20

**Purpose:** Build the ruled coverage batch: callout ledger + gate, skills-parked/ with two-way check and twice-counter, /intake and /probe prototypes, seat.sh, the covered/skipped done-box row.

**Insights:**

1. callouts.sh gate had a same-second tie bug (pass < claim false when timestamps equal); fixed to <= so ties fail closed. Ledger_ts is 1-second resolution; any gate comparing its timestamps needs a tie rule.
2. zsh does not word-split an unquoted $CMD variable; test harnesses that alias a script must use a function, not a string variable.
3. The parked match verb keys tags to cheap file probes (xcodeproj, next.config.*, package.json); a match is a suggestion the agent weighs, never an auto-copy — the nudge box says so in its arrow line.
4. The friction twice-rule is enforced at write time (the add verb itself announces the second occurrence), so the asker cannot forget to check.
5. Roster went 96 → 88 live skills; 11 parked with tldr+tags index.

---

**Purpose:** Render the Versable Foundry contract summary (365-line source, ten decisions, 16 fenced blocks) as an 11-page design note.

**Insights:**

1. Measure fence widths in characters, not bytes. `awk`'s `length()` reported 184 and 203 columns for diagrams that are really 73 and 84, because box-drawing glyphs are 3 bytes each. A byte measurement makes every diagram look unfixable; the Python character pass named the five blocks that actually breached the 78/84 gates.
2. The unsplittable-block gap is fixable by author order, not by flags. A 24-line JSON listing left 45% of a page blank; moving the section's short diagram AND its why-paragraph ahead of the listing cut the gap to under 20%.
3. A `Table:` caption immediately after a code block renders as that code block's caption, two italic lines deep. Put one sentence of prose between them, or drop the caption and let the sentence introduce the table.
4. `\newpage` before a level-1 heading whose first content is a 21-line diagram converts an accidental half-page into a deliberate section break.
5. A markdown table row with an empty cell is a shape error the source can carry invisibly and the renderer cannot. Four capability ids with notes on two of them is a bullet list plus a lead sentence.
6. lint.py's two standing false positives on this document: a noun triad naming three distinct attributed things, and "how many" read as an unquantified size.

- New commit-subject trap: **the release PR title can collide with an already-published version**. PR #279 is titled "Release v5.2.5" while `RELEASE-NOTES-v5.2.5.md` already exists for PR #269, whose real title is "Release V5.2.4-b". Check `gh pr view <prev> --json title` against the existing notes filename before naming the output; do not trust either one alone. Filed the run under `release-v-<ver>-pr<N>/` so nothing was overwritten.
- New commit-subject trap: **"test: prune excessive tests" is a net test reduction**, not cleanup. Commit `55f3826d` cut 324 lines and added 143, including 215 lines off the test for the release's largest new surface. A `test:` prefix reads as neutral maintenance; run `git show <sha> --stat` on any test commit before summarising it.
- The "moved gate, not removed gate" trap recurred in a third costume. `guardCronRequest(req)` became `guardCronRequest(req, secret)`, which reads as hardening, but both callers still pass the same `process.env.CRON_SECRET`. It enables per-route secrets without introducing any. State what a signature change makes possible separately from what it currently does.
- The doc-inflation check from v5.2.4 paid off again: 548 files collapsed to 108 code files once `docs/`, `.claude/` and `*.md` were excluded. Worth running as step 1 every time, since the headline file count is the number a reader anchors on.
- zsh gotcha while reading refs: `git show "$H:frontend/..."` silently loses the `:f`, producing `origin/developmentontend/...`. zsh applied a parameter modifier. Use literal refs (`origin/development:path`) rather than a variable followed by a colon.

## word-doc: first document, the meta-skills audit [valid-docx-7a] — 2026-08-19

**Purpose:** Build the skill and prove it on a real document (the /validate audit of the meta-skills, 5 pages, 6 tables, 1 diagram, 3 callouts, TOC).

**Insights:**

1. Equal-width pipe-table columns were the first visible defect on a real document (a "#" column as wide as the sentence column). The filter now sizes columns from content and guarantees each column its longest word; unequal dash counts still override.
2. A fence info string with options but no braces (```python caption="x") is not a fence to pandoc; the whole block became inline text. Preflight now errors on it; the contract is ```{.python caption="x"}.
3. Word's TOC field ships empty to Google Docs and LibreOffice. The static hyperlinked contents list the filter builds renders everywhere; it has no page numbers, which is the trade.
4. LibreOffice keeps heading + first paragraph + following table together more eagerly than Word, so the preview shows gaps Word will not. Diagram and code boxes (keepLines) cause real gaps; author order around them.
5. The ink colour must live in docDefaults, not on Normal, or the table header's white text loses to the paragraph style in Word's cascade.
6. Google Docs' handling of Consolas is UNCONFIRMED; check on the first Drive upload and record here.

## deck: skill built, first deck, reviewer baseline · 2026-08-18 20:15
**Purpose:** Build /deck fast per the owner's brief (content in the agent's hands, everything else in scripts), then baseline the reviewer on the three peer decks.

**Insights:**
1. A deterministic markdown→HTML renderer beat "make it a create-report style": create-report's pipeline has the agent parse markdown into JSON, which is exactly the scaffolding the owner wanted out of the agent's hands. Recorded as a deviation from spec v2 §2, with reason.
2. `.body{overflow:hidden}` is what makes the in-page overflow measurement honest; without it scrollHeight==clientHeight for every slide and the check cannot fail.
3. Chrome `--dump-dom` with `?check=1` is a zero-dependency way to get a real layout measurement out of a static file; `--virtual-time-budget` is needed or the JS has not run.
4. The reviewer's sensitivity is a seat question: sonnet-low found the same 3 contradictions as an opus pass on the gcp deck and 0 of its 16 overstatements. Default sonnet-low, offer opus under --deep.
5. All three peer decks failed on the same class: a fact that moved after the deck was written. The reviewer prompt now says to check source mtime against the deck first.

**Purpose:** Owner-directed evening: make the session goal survive /clear with a structured box; rebuild /tasks as the grouped default; write path for builds with no Task tool; deck spec v2.

**Insights:**

4. block-nested-claude.sh fires on the literal text `.claude/` in a heredoc even when the write target is `$VIEW_DIR`; route long patches through a scratchpad file written with the Write tool.
5. `while read` over `printf '%s'` drops the last unterminated line: the segment loop in guard-secret-file-read.sh silently judged nothing until `printf '%s\n'`.

## session: round 2 fold executed, items 1 to 3 (the door, the trust lane, the cheap future bump) [vb-fable-e4] · 2026-08-18

**Purpose:** on the owner's "go", land the forward-facing third of the magi findings: AGENTS.md rerouted, counts derived or deleted, `docs/INSTALL.md`, named table exports, the kit's first test suite and two CI gates, the upgrade runbook and changelog shipped in the package. Commits `cf0d756`, `6030b2d`, `c83f32a`, board `d098ad1`; not pushed.

**Insights:**
1. The owner reframed the value question and it changed the plan more than the findings: "no consumer yet" is a measurement date the scripture already sets (C4), not a verdict, so the work is the on-ramp and the trust lane, never the bump. I had recommended the bump against a ruling in my own briefing fences (atone `mist-20260817-203006-ed`); the precheck is to quote any fence a recommendation touches before making it.
2. Vite 8 ignores the `esbuild` key; the kit's `jsx: preserve` tsconfig has to be overridden through `oxc: { jsx, tsconfigRaw }` for vitest to parse the kit's TSX. Tests live in `test/` outside `src/` so `pnpm typecheck` never sees vitest globals.
3. A render smoke over "every capitalized export that is a function or has $$typeof" mounted 57 components; sixteen needed minimal props and the props table records exactly why each row exists. The barrel snapshot is what catches a removed export; the mount catches a component that throws. Both were mutation-tested (FacetBar removed, Kicker made to throw) before the commit.
4. Regenerating DO-NOTS produced no diff, so "one commit stale" in the fold was recency, not content; the CI diff step is still right because it makes that distinction mechanical.
5. Rewriting AGENTS.md shifted every line citation into it; the governing docs cite AGENTS.md twelve times and all twelve needed re-pointing before the ratchet held. Any structural rewrite of a cited file is a citation sweep too.
6. `git add` enumeration warnings fired three times; the tree carried two never-stage files (the owner's speedway-todo.md, the runtime notes), so enumeration was the safe shape and was dismissed each time with the reason.

## session: review round 2, the magi panel on usability, value add and gaps (#93), seven access-partitioned seats and a jester [vb-fable-e4] · 2026-08-17

**Purpose:** resume from `_20260817-catch-tail-c4.claude.md`; the owner redirected the magi from the deck to the project itself and asked for a jester who holds that agentic coding is doomed, plus seats with code-only, docs-only, code+docs and front-doors-only access. Ran full mode with seven opus seats, an anonymized vote, a verified fold, and filed the dispositions on the board (`3e67bd5`, not pushed). Archive `~/.claude/assets/magi/20260817-2028-vb-usability-value-gaps`.

**Insights:**
1. Access partitions did two jobs at once: they satisfied magi's independence gate (seven primary bases, no shared digest) and turned "usability" into a measurement. The site-only seat found the missing install path, the front-doors seat found the enforcement living outside the repo, the apps-only seat found the pin history refuting "deliberate lag"; the all-access seat could confirm each but had not led with any of them.
2. Handing the seats the supervisor's own "this is good" claims as tear targets, and keeping one expected finding off the list as a discovery signal, produced sharper output than an open review: every P-row got a verdict with evidence, and the withheld build-versus-buy gap was reached only by the jester's path-not-taken, which is exactly the seat it should have come from.
3. The jester on opus (a named deviation from the design's opposite-model rule) earned its seat: it found the `export *` hole no other seat saw and conceded proportion, not kind. Same-model was the right call for a premise attack that had to survive a scored vote; the setup-check WARN is the price and it was worth naming.
4. Background seats return only idle notices; the abstracts and `<usage>` blocks never reach the parent, so per-seat cost was unrecordable and `cost-estimate.sh` reports 0. Next run: dispatch seats in the foreground for the last one, or ask each seat to append its usage line into its own file.
5. The aggregator expects real voter ids in the score keys and does not read the anon map; un-map into `voter-N-scores.json` yourself and keep the anonymized ballots under another name pattern.
6. The checkpoint's Resume line named two candidate magi subjects and told me to ask if the first message did not settle it; I planned on my own carried default instead and the owner had to correct me (atone `mist-20260817-145035-63`, S2). When a checkpoint names two candidates, the ask is one line and it goes first.
7. The card the owner asked for came after the dispatch instead of before it. Deliver the small requested artifact before starting the long one; the order was the whole complaint.

## core-dump: sealing the two-day gcc-work marathon — 2026-08-16 05:10

**Purpose:** Full dump before running a 5-task autonomous batch, carrying the
store-resolution trap and the uncommitted state across the clear.

**Insights:**

1. Seed Pending Items from the TASK STORE, not from memory, and pin the session.
   This dump's own subject matter is a resolver that reads the wrong store on a
   bare call; a core-dump that seeded from `ls -t` would have inherited another
   session's backlog into the checkpoint.
2. Standing constraints grew to five because three owner rulings landed in one
   session (table height, dereference-every-reference, route-around-a-bad-channel).
   Rulings arrive faster than they graduate into rules/, and the Resume Contract is
   where they live in between.
3. The caveat list is the honest half. Two days uncommitted, a permanent junk row
   in an append-only store with no recovery path, and a half-migrated hook batch are
   all things a summary would smooth away. They lead the contract for that reason.
4. Recording that OUTSIDE READERS found both shipped defects is worth a line in the
   insights. It is the strongest signal in the session about where verification was
   weak, and it is invisible in any test output.
